prospect.name: Sankalp Shetty
prospect.occupation: Physician. Quit his job roughly three and a half months ago and is currently interviewing for new positions.
prospect.training_background: Formerly very active — swimming, table tennis, cricket, bodyweight training, and could do 70-80 push-ups in a single set. Since 2019 essentially nothing; currently 3,000-4,000 steps a day plus stretching for his lower back, lower limb and left shoulder. Cannot hold a plank or push-up position for 5-10 seconds.
prospect.medical: Extensive and active. Left frozen shoulder first diagnosed 2019 with MRI showing supraspinatus grade 1 tear, AC joint osteoarthritis and joint effusion; recurred after a second injury, treated with several months of physiotherapy each time; left scapular region still markedly weak. Two falls roughly five to six months apart caused by numbness in the right leg. Whole-spine MRI showing degeneration at C5-C6, T10-T11 and L5-S1 discs, plus facet joint arthritis and sacroiliac involvement. Psoriatic lesions on the palms diagnosed early 2026, leading to a final diagnosis of a psoriatic arthritic attack — 'I'm like currently undergoing treatment'. A recent MRI shows a new L4-L5 disc protrusion that was not present four months earlier. Gained 10-12 kg in six to seven months, then lost 8 kg through treatment. Left piriformis weak.

signals: In the middle of an active diagnosis and treatment, not recovering from a past one: 'the final conclusion came that it was a psoriatic arthritic attack which I had. So, got myself treated for that also, I'm like currently undergoing treatment'
New pathology appearing while he waits: 'it has like got a disc protrusion also, and the L5 L4, L5 level, which was not there previously, 4 months ago, but currently it has started'
Frames training as the way through the illness: 'I wanted to know how we could work through all these things, if I'm continuing with, or if I start with kettlebell exercise'

Overlaps with the_rebuilder — he wants a former self back ('earlier, I used to do almost like 70 to 80 push-ups in a single rod') — but the deciding factor is that he is mid-episode and mid-treatment, not post-episode
Departs from the archetype on one axis: motivation is high but he has no money, having spent his savings on treatment

goals.text: Understand whether he can safely do kettlebell training at all given his spine and shoulder
Rebuild strength in his left shoulder and scapular region so he can hold a plank and push-up position again
Resolve the stiffness in his lower back and the weakness in his left piriformis
Get back to being as active as he was before 2019

pains.text: Recurrent frozen shoulder with a supraspinatus tear and AC joint osteoarthritis; left shoulder 'absolutely weak'
Multi-level spinal disc degeneration with a new L4-L5 protrusion appearing in the last four months, plus facet and sacroiliac arthritis
Two falls caused by right leg numbness, of initially unexplained origin
Cannot hold a push-up or plank position for even 5-10 seconds, having previously done 70-80 push-ups per set
Shift work of 24 to 48 hours straight destroyed any possibility of a training routine for years
Savings exhausted by medical treatment and currently unemployed

objections.raw_quote: The reason I would, I'm hesitant to start today is, because as I told, I'm short on budget right now, I'm short on the currency right now, and I'm looking for other jobs.
objections.rep_response: Ran the 'life only gets busier' timing challenge once, then asked twice more what he could put down today, got a flat 'No', and ended the call without presenting anything.

objections.raw_quote: if I keep aside like maybe 10,000, that would be around 60,000 Indian rupees... So it will be around 600 USDs... 600 overall, across six months.
objections.rep_response: Did not correct the anchor or state the actual price. Told him there was no use in going through the offer if they would have to wait a month anyway.

evidence: Rep financially disqualified before presenting: 'we, of course, always start with an investment, and it depends on how specifically we would approach it, and I would know that at the end of a meeting like this, but there is no use case in going into all of that right now, if we need to wait another month anyway.'
Prospect committed to a specific date to re-engage: 'the 15th of July is what I have booked for now' and agreed to message on WhatsApp.
Rep put the onus on the prospect to reach out: 'I want you to also take that commitment for yourself.'

Counter-evidence on the follow-up being real: the prospect has no job, no savings and a stated six-month budget of about $600 against a $6,000 programme — a tenfold gap that a month of employment will not close.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to text on WhatsApp on 15 July once employed, at which point a new call would be booked. Rep sent him a kettlebell workout video in the meantime.

notable.note: The single most serious clinical exposure in the batch. A physician disclosed, in the first four minutes and in clinical detail, an unrepaired supraspinatus tear, degeneration at C5-C6, T10-T11 and L5-S1, a new L4-L5 protrusion, two falls from right-leg numbness, and active treatment for psoriatic arthritis. The rep asked no clearance question, made no referral, and closed the call by sending him a video of 'the best kettle belts workouts that you can actually be doing' and telling him to 'start maybe doing a few exercises'. Separately, this is the call the sales coach reviewed the following day, criticising the rep only for having qualified on money too early — the clinical picture was never mentioned in that review.

quality.notes: Severe inversion in the middle third. Whole rep questions are attributed to SANKALP SHETTY, including the entire financial-qualification sequence at 00:08:32-00:09:44 ('And just to have an idea, would that be something you could do at the moment already') and the disqualification at 00:12:35. Roles resolved from content.
